newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Waigel says he optimistic jobs deal obtaintable.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says he optimistic jobs deal obtaintable.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Sunday he was "cautiously optimistic" that there would be an agreement with France on employment strategy at the European Union summit meeting.

Speaking in a live interview with ZDF television of Germany, Waigel said EU leaders were working on resolving their differnces on Sunday and would continue their efforts early on Monday. But he insisted that there would be no additional spending for a jobs scheme.
"We have been working on this for days," Waigel said. "We will try today and continue working tomorrow morning. I am cautiously optimistic. But we have quite a bit still to take care of."

Waigel said neither France nor Germany were interested in setting up costly bureaucracies that would ursurp the powers of national governments to fight unemployment. He said France had no interest in deficit-spending schemes to lower unemployment.

"We are not against an employment chapter in the treaty, but we do not want anything that will supercede national authorities," Waigel said. "We don't want new authorities. There is no money for that. We already pay enough. The basic philosophy has to be -- local solutions to global thinking."

He added: "Employment policies have to remain the responsibility of the states...The French are also not demanding additional authorities or credit-financed spending programmes, but rather a strengthened coordination. We have to see that we reach a reasonable result. The stability pact cannot be undermined or affected in any way. Not a single comma or decimal point can be changed."
